observerCalibration.scope: Two observer ON/OFF pairs per library, full-stream rolling-logs only; previously independently reviewed.
priorLimits: R02 prospectively passes full PNG equality and repairs screenshot timing without masking or changing terminal policy. Original native calibration bytes match the prior independent review and old rejected xterm arms remain rejected. Only two full-stream rolling pairs per library were calibrated; no material aggregate perturbation was observed, not zero overhead or an equivalence bound. R02 first OFF arm ends at load 5.61; subsequent ON admission waited about 45 seconds until load 3.71.

The logical endpoint is reset plus paced writes, two RAFs, and direct target snapshots. There is no GL fence, device-completion, or physical presentation proof. Post-window text, hashing, settlement, and screenshots do not enter the measured counters.

Snapshots are sequential and non-atomic. PID/type/start identities agree at both endpoints, but a process born and gone entirely between endpoints is unobservable. The Python reader and Node driver are outside allChrome.

contextFromPriorIndependentReview.interpretation: Unicode/emoji and line-scroll energy/instruction losses remain real under their reviewed instrumented protocols. fairnessAndLimits.text: Equal final history rows and text do not establish equal intermediate retained state. The perturbative Linux Unicode proof gives native 2.3726588154% fewer mean retained history rows and 2.3728449203% fewer RAF-interval-weighted rows. That is a potentially favorable retained-state exposure for ghostty, not a conservative condition by row exposure. The actual Mac Unicode trajectory and its causal contribution to instructions or energy are unobserved.

The later Mac trajectory is rolling-logs (ASCII), not rolling-unicode-logs. Its native/xterm mean ratio 1.0535329082366438 cannot be substituted for Unicode or used to claim conservative Unicode bias. Linux trajectories are mechanism evidence, not Mac efficiency windows. Row counts are not a linear CPU/energy cost model; no synthetic retention adjustment is justified.

Prior independently reviewed observer calibration covered only two full-stream rolling-logs pairs per library. No material aggregate perturbation was observed there; it provides neither workload-specific bounded-Unicode calibration nor an equivalence bound. This review qualifies the instrumented descriptive condition, not an observer-free efficiency estimate. No observer-overhead subtraction is applied.

ri_energy_nj is the kernel estimate of CPU energy for enumerated stable Chrome processes. It excludes physical GPU-device energy, display, other-process power and battery life. The GPU channel measures Chrome GPU-process CPU work. Logical completion uses reset, paced writes, two RAFs and direct target snapshots; there is no GL fence, device-completion or physical-presentation proof. Post-window text readback, SHA-256, 1600 ms settlement and screenshots are outside the counters.

Snapshots are sequential and non-atomic. PID/type/start identities match and reads succeed at both endpoints, but a process born and gone entirely between them is unobservable. The Python reader and Node driver are outside allChrome. Native/CDP CPU agreement is a consistency check, not a proof of atomic or complete lifetime accounting.

The frozen efficiency driver lacks the newer per-window owned-helper capability metadata described in the current reader contract. The reader has independent M1 ABI/units/fixed-work validation, and every measured window has positive aggregate instruction, cycle, P-work and energy deltas. These support the observed historical channels; idle-process zeros must not be labelled unsupported. This is not certification that the historical driver satisfied the newer startup-metadata contract.

The retained-text oracle symmetrically trims trailing whitespace. Hidden-history cell styles are outside it. Full retained-line arrays were not stored, so a fresh independent offline full-history rehash is unavailable; equality rests on recorded full-history SHA-256, equal row counts, matching stored head/tail and reviewed readback code. Renderer-owned canvas width/height are the actual recorded drawing-canvas backing attributes, with matching xterm device-canvas dimensions, not independently measured GPU memory allocations or separately stored GL drawingBufferWidth/Height.

AC/load checks and the available turn ledger pass, with no recorded overlapping Mac turn. They do not establish continuous thermal or non-Chrome workload isolation. The retained artifacts show one acquisition and all eight registered windows; they cannot prove absence of hypothetical unlogged acquisitions. Custody is scoped to the supplied owned-process receipt, not unrelated owner processes.

Four balanced pairs from one headed Chrome 154 session on one Apple M1 at 17 terminals are descriptive observations, not statistical or cross-machine equivalence. This prospective current-runtime condition does not causally attribute differences to historical source changes and does not rescore older evidence. It is neither a universal WebGL superiority claim nor a qualification of a shipped optimization; the previously reviewed Unicode/emoji, line-scroll and edit results still accompany project-level claims.

findings.finding: All four registered ghostty/xterm pairs are lower for ghostty in native CPU, instructions, cycles and estimated all-Chrome CPU energy. Exact median ratios are CPU 0.765304505089796, instructions 0.6892012798406932, cycles 0.7775755586056233 and energy 0.7300621262510423. The corrected wave target screen passes for this condition; CPU-only is diagnostic.

Registration precedes acquisition, all eight windows are retained, and 136 target-windows have identical public input/write work, matching final 9572 history rows and retained-text hashes, real renderer-owned 560x456 canvas backing, successful stable PID/type/start snapshots, passing host guards and clean supplied custody. Sealed assets, pinned source inventories, run log and raw archive agree.

Final equality does not equal identical retained work over time. The Linux Unicode proof has native mean row exposure 0.9762734118462156x xterm, potentially favoring ghostty; no Mac Unicode trajectory or causal cost correction exists. The later Mac +5.3533% mean trajectory is ASCII and cannot establish conservative Unicode bias.

Qualification is for the instrumented matched-final condition and estimated enumerated-Chrome CPU energy only. Direct bounded-Unicode observer calibration, full retained-line offline rehash, GPU-device completion/energy and complete between-endpoint process coverage are absent. Prior Unicode/emoji and line-scroll losses remain relevant to the project verdict.
